basis: Congenital cleft directly affects the upper lip/oral structures and maxillary bone; associated CNS and nasal abnormalities are variable.
Benign neoplasm arising in adrenal cortex; hormone excess occurs in functional subtypes and does not define the entire group.
Acquired distal tubular acidification defect defines both renal dysfunction and metabolic acidosis; underlying diseases are not additional organ involvement.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects marrow and myeloid blood cells; other KIT-associated tumors are separate diseases.
Defined by reversed heart and abdominal organ positions, usually with normal function; pulmonary situs also reverses but is omitted under the primary cap.
Peripheral neuropathy and glomerulosclerotic nephropathy define the syndrome; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 4/12 patients.
Thyroid inflammation; autoimmune and immune-mediated forms predominate, although the umbrella also includes radiation-induced thyroiditis.
Developmental impairment defines the syndrome; dental defects/caries 80-99%, scoliosis/contractures 30-79%, strabismus 30-79%; cardiac defects 5-29%.
Clonal hematopoietic neoplasms with eosinophilia; lymphoma presentations and eosinophilic damage to other organs are not established across most subtypes.
Acute inflammation of the tympanic membrane, usually caused by viral or bacterial infection.
Neuroepithelial tumor of mature ganglion cells; hemianopia reflects central visual pathway involvement, while endocrine abnormalities are occasional.
Microcephaly, brain malformations and developmental disability with primordial skeletal growth disorder and frequent contractures; renal and hearing defects 5-29%.
Severe skeletal dysplasia with narrow thorax; sustained respiratory dysfunction is common and causes death in most patients during early infancy.
Developmental disability, polydactyly and cutaneous hemangiomas are defining features; cardiac and urogenital defects lack evidence of common involvement.
Glycerol metabolism defect; developmental impairment annotated at 80-99%; myopathy/adrenal hypoplasia suggest complex Xp21 deletion rather than isolated GKD.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Cerebellar degeneration and ataxia; eye movement findings are neurologic. Digit morphology alone does not establish damage; hypogonadism/hearing loss are occasional.
Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis is an immune/complement-mediated glomerular disease; no common extrarenal damage is established.
Genetic bone development disorder with multiple metaphyseal enchondromas; lesions occupy skeletal tissue despite the benign course.
Broad reproductive testicular disease category; endocrine dysfunction, infection and hematologic tumors apply only to subsets.
Disordered activation of mast cells, a hematopoietic immune-cell lineage; episodic skin, gut and cardiovascular symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage.
Scalp aplasia 10/11, enamel hypoplasia 9/9 and developmental delay 7/9 define the syndrome; cataracts directly affect the eye in 5/10.
Congenital optic disc malformation with impaired vision; optic nerve involvement belongs to the ocular axis. Extraocular anomalies are not consistently common.
Malignancy originates in the reproductive ovary; endocrine effects occur only in selected sex cord-stromal subtypes.
Inherited thyroid hormone metabolism abnormality with elevated reverse T3 and rT3/T3 ratio in 8/8; no common damage to another organ is documented.
